items.title: Atomic activate-plan via RPC
items.notes: Currently deactivateUserWorkoutPlans + updateUserWorkoutPlan/createUserWorkoutPlan are two separate round-trips. A parallel client (multi-device) could race between them. Wrap both in a Postgres SECURITY DEFINER function activate_user_workout_plan(plan_id) that runs the deactivate+activate in one transaction. Low priority — single-device users won't hit this.

items.title: Calendar view: past logs + future planned workouts
items.notes: Single calendar surface that shows: (a) past dates with logged workouts (link to session detail), and (b) upcoming dates with the active plan's scheduled sessions per plan_schedule. Likely a dedicated tab or screen, not a modal — the heatmap on History only shows volume, not a day-by-day workout-name view. Source data: workout_sessions for past, active user_workout_plan + plan_schedule for future. Probably wants month + week views.

items.title: Login + Onboarding UI polish
items.notes: Tighten the login screen to match the honest-mirror design system (anthracite base, mono caps, strava-orange CTA) and add a 2-3 screen onboarding flow for first-time signups. Onboarding: (a) intro/value prop, (b) optional goal pick (strength/hypertrophy/general), (c) jump straight into Browse Plans with the 4 standard plans pre-filtered. Login screen items: Apple sign-in button (iOS), Google button styling once OAuth is enabled in Supabase, password reset flow, helpful errors instead of raw Supabase messages. See feedback_pr_workflow / DESIGN.md for tokens.

items.title: Auth integration automation toolkit
items.notes: Reduce per-project auth setup to a single command. Today every new app repeats: configure Google/Apple OAuth client in their consoles, add redirect URIs, paste client IDs into Supabase Auth providers, set Supabase Site URL + Redirect allow-list to the app scheme, wire useAuth + expo-auth-session, add Apple sign-in entitlement, handle deep-link callback. Goal: a hyperfit-auth-kit (script + template) that (a) prompts for app scheme + bundle id, (b) generates the useAuth hook + login screen pre-styled per DESIGN.md, (c) writes the correct Supabase URL config via the management API, (d) optionally provisions Google OAuth client via gcloud + Apple service ID via App Store Connect API, (e) writes .env.example entries and app.json scheme/entitlements. Stretch: a doctor command that diagnoses the localhost-redirect class of bugs by reading Supabase config + app.json and reporting mismatches. Reference: this project's hyperfit:// scheme, EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_* env vars, src/hooks/useAuth.ts.

items.title: Plan moderation queue + admin approve/reject workflow
items.notes: When a user taps PUBLISH on their plan, it flips review_status from 'private' to 'pending_review' but there is no surface to act on the queue. Build: (a) admin-only listing of workout_plans where review_status='pending_review' (RPC list_pending_plans or a view + admin RLS), (b) approve_plan(plan_id) RPC that sets review_status='approved' + is_public=true, (c) reject_plan(plan_id, reason) RPC that sets review_status='rejected' + writes review_notes, (d) minimal admin UI (in-app dev screen guarded by an admin claim, or a Supabase SQL snippet/CLI script for now). Today plans submitted via PUBLISH pile up forever. Reference: src/services/workoutService.ts setPlanReviewStatus + usePlanActions submitForReview/withdrawFromReview. UI side: WorkoutPlansLibrary already shows PUBLISH/RESUBMIT/WITHDRAW buttons keyed off review_status, so once the backend exists no client work is needed for the basic flow.

items.title: Revisit signup enumeration UX vs anti-enumeration tradeoff
items.notes: useAuth.signUpWithEmail surfaces alreadyExists:true based on Supabase's empty-identities response, and LoginView shows 'An account with this email already exists.' This is a deliberate UX call (clear feedback for users who forgot they signed up) but defeats Supabase's anti-enumeration default — an attacker can probe whether an email is registered via signup attempts. Acceptable today (Supabase rate-limits signups, low user count, low value as an enumeration target) but worth revisiting if (a) user growth makes the email list more valuable, (b) we add a public registration form without captcha, or (c) compliance review flags it. Mitigations: keep current UX but add captcha/turnstile on signup, OR fall back to generic 'Check your email for a confirmation link' for both cases. Reference: src/hooks/useAuth.ts:62-68, src/components/LoginView.tsx, /gstack-review on PR #48.

items.title: Real AI workout recommender
items.notes: AI SUGGESTION buttons hidden across WorkoutPlanner (rest-day branch + active-day branch) and EmptyWorkoutCard. The previous action seeded a hardcoded AI_SEED list, not a real model. When reinstated, drive from: (a) recent session history (workout_sessions + workout_sets), (b) the user's active plan + day-of-week, (c) muscle group fatigue (muscle_volume_view), (d) optionally a small LLM call. Surface points: rest-day callout on Plans tab, EmptyWorkoutCard for users without an active plan, in-session 'next exercise' nudge.
